proof_boundary: Formal contracts plus reviewed implementation/test correspondence; not compiler refinement or native dependency proof.

model-probe.obligation: Each test sends its fixed sample using the selected provider and endpoint. An ASR test uses the engine and credential captured for that request.
model-probe.assumptions: The models cover request identity and credential ownership. Transport tests exercise sample contents and response parsing. Provider availability is external.

online-asr-identity.obligation: Credential edits require a confirmed engine and Alibaba current-epoch endpoint; GLM shares its slot and local engines have no credential slot. Read retry preserves committed engine changes, independent key failure preserves endpoint success, obsolete endpoint completions cannot publish, and debounced writes retain captured identity across a flush-before-switch boundary.
online-asr-identity.assumptions: Three engine kinds with representative Alibaba-domestic/GLM-international combinations, three read batches within two configuration contexts, at most one engine mutation and one read-only retry, two edit/clear attempts and two write invocations. Only a committed engine switch changes context. Retry reissues ERROR fields; READY and PENDING siblings retain their context and may publish after retry. Native success/failure and response order are environmental inputs. Aggregate switch reads settle on first failure or both successes; pending sibling callbacks remain enabled. Engine, endpoint and key failures expose recoverable errors; a key failure preserves identity and an accepted edit retires old key results and clears its key error. Expected identity and write ledgers are independent of implementation readiness. Timer dispatch is abstract in TLC; real hook replay checks 599/600 ms, URL/readiness publication, first-failure busy release, selective retry and deferred flush completion. Switch with both an in-flight save and a second pending draft is excluded and left to debouncer unit regressions. Reachability witnesses are intentional negations, not safety proofs. Region mutation, catalogs, unmount lifecycle, backend storage internals and other windows are outside this bounded companion; no whole-source refinement claim.

engine-status-ownership.obligation: A newer status query or accepted funasr-status event retires older status snapshots. Obsolete status results and errors cannot publish stage, device, GPU or error, start the engine or stop current polling. An accepted missing-model status offers a download and retains the current polling state. Only user action starts a model download. A separate start owner survives native loading progress and running/not-ready polling; a new actual start or accepted terminal state retires it. Three current start rejections reach terminal error and retire pending status queries, preserving that error against late loading. Already issued starts remain issued. Current queries and post-crash recovery still publish.
engine-status-ownership.assumptions: Finite safety companion with independent snapshot and native-start ownership. General bound: three queries, one external ready/loading/missing/error/crashed event and one native loading progress event per issued start. Progress bound: six ordered stopped/loading queries, three native loading events and three rejected starts. Each start spans a loading poll; the last poll completes after terminal start error. Specification snapshot/start epochs are independent of implementation tokens. Obsolete status/start completions remain enabled. The polling flag represents the real 6000 ms interval; loading retains prior polling, ready/error stop it, crash immediately queries and starts polling. The model checks status notifications before any user download input. Issued start ledgers cannot be undone. Five faults cover query retirement, event retirement, awaited-start catch ownership, start retirement on loading progress, and an implicit download on missing status. Two separately labeled reachability witnesses require current error followed by ready recovery (post-crash recovery is checked by implementation replay) and all three legitimate start failures despite progress/polls plus a dropped late loading snapshot; neither witness is a safety negative. Genuine TLC State schedules replay renderHook, deferred API calls and captured listener, checking public metadata/stage/error, timer and side-effect counts. The ten-loading restart threshold is covered by implementation tests; download generations, cancellation, unmount, other model-state branches, native scheduling, unbounded requests, refinement and liveness are outside this model.

history-stats.obligation: Only the latest started statistics request may publish or log a failure. A current failure retains the last accepted statistics, including when an older success arrives later; a later current success recovers. Unmount retires pending completions.
history-stats.assumptions: Three ordered request identities with success/error as environment inputs; starts abstract mount, history-updated, delete and reprocess refreshes. Actual publication/error ledgers are compared with independent latest-started intent. One unmount invalidates pending work. The reachability witness requires current error logging, accepted recovery and disposal with pending work; it is not a safety negative. TLC counterexample schedules replay the actual page via the API and captured event listener, asserting distinct DOM metrics and console errors. Bounded correspondence only; no unbounded-request, React/native scheduling, refinement or liveness proof. React drops state after unmount, so cleanup replay observes a rejected pending promise instead.

recording.obligation: Reserve, cancel, stop and publish only the current recording session; final UI events cannot regress; disposed recording listeners cannot act. Explicit dictation polish skip is restricted to the current positive processing-session identity; stale cancellation and cleanup cannot affect a newer session.
recording.assumptions: CPAL/OS capture and scheduler termination are environmental inputs; two sessions in TLC, Nat ownership contracts in Lean. Session-scoped polish skip and output-timing publication are checked by deterministic implementation tests and source correspondence; existing lifecycle models do not establish source refinement for these additions.

capture.obligation: Native handoff is accepted once; CPAL fallback owns its samples; cap samples and snapshot the selected device.
capture.assumptions: Audio driver success and sample values are inputs; bounded samples represent arbitrary content; RecordingOwnsMonitor begins after the synchronous stop, not the earlier slot reservation.

monitor.obligation: Stop invalidates pending starts; recording ownership prevents late idle-monitor publication; disposed effects never restart monitoring. Monitor restart rechecks active/enabled/mounted/recording/current generation after awaits; late native start is compensated; only the newest overlapping test may resume.
monitor.assumptions: Driver initialization can take time and must observe cancellation; the property guards publication, not an instantaneous hardware shutdown guarantee. Two independent microphone test requests with out-of-order success/failure, one intent retirement and serialized stop/start/compensation phases. Native stop eventually settles; physical instantaneous shutdown is not asserted. A second companion separates two hook instances, a shared native-operation queue, late first start compensation and retired test completion; global native ownership prevents retired cleanup from stopping its replacement.

engine.obligation: Engine/directory changes respect busy capture/download; late starts cannot publish; cloud readiness uses its captured key slot. Present invalid completion metadata is authoritative corrupt state even with a large weight; absent metadata retains legacy compatibility; corrupt/missing status offers explicit repair, and a verified repair becomes ready. Concurrent engine.json field updates preserve committed independent fields and release the transaction after failure.
engine.assumptions: Four engine classes; model output correctness and filesystem/driver/network primitives are outside proof. Ready/error values are environmental inputs. Cache integrity companion partitions absent/valid/invalid manifest and absent/large weights. A positive trace witness reaches repair completion; this reachability target is deliberately false and is not a safety proof. Actual replay calls cache resolvers and explicit download_model verification/atomic manifest publication on temporary local bytes; no GPU/model inference internals are claimed. Configuration writes are within one application process; four independent fields and atomic replacement success/failure are modeled. External writers and arbitrary filesystem durability are outside the mutex contract. Audio-processing reads observe engine.json; writes reuse the reviewed update_engine_json transaction helper. EngineConfigurationWrites retains exactly four writers with one update each; the additional enhancement field and its interleavings are implementation correspondence, not enumerated model states. Startup bootstrap/reconciliation, positive acknowledgement, persistence rollback, UI behavior and enhancer reconstruction are covered by implementation review and regression tests, not dedicated formal proofs. Python enhancement lifecycle regressions mock model/device/enhancer operations and do not independently establish dispatch-lock exclusion or DSP correctness.

download.obligation: A cancelled download retains ownership/configuration until worker termination; cleanup cannot release a newer task; cancellation/unmount revoke frontend timers and old asynchronous callbacks. Frontend promises and status events require the active request identity. Scoped cancellation cannot signal a replacement task, and every cancellation acknowledgement follows worker termination, terminal publication and owned-slot release, including preparation, progress and child-wait stages.
download.assumptions: Filesystem writes and HTTP completion are environmental outcomes; scheduler fairness is required for worker settlement. DownloadTaskEventOwnership bounds two request identities, up to two cancellation waiters per request, preparation/progress/child-wait phases, all four status classes and late promise settlement. Request identities are unique across hook lifetimes; identity-less legacy events cannot own a scoped frontend attempt. Native process, filesystem and HTTP outcomes are inputs. CancellationFinishes assumes weak fairness for cancellation observation, terminal publication and cleanup; it gives no wall-clock bound. Native worker tests inject local child/preparation outcomes. These finite contracts are not compiler refinement. Cancellation while waiting for lifecycle may finish before preparation starts. Started engine preparation is not dropped: cancellation retains the slot until its future and blocking extraction settle, then suppresses child spawn. Progress assumes preparation, kill and reap eventually finish; no wall-clock cancellation bound is proved.

directory.obligation: Copy before committing destination; never delete source until current destination and runtime readiness are rechecked.
directory.assumptions: Canonical path resolution and successful copies are trusted filesystem operations; source deletion failures must remain visible.

discovery.obligation: Only the newest request for current provider/engine/auth context may publish; failure retains same-context data. Selective invalidation retires and clears only the selected catalog; polish publication preserves independent assistant ownership and shared catalogs follow polish. Context, authentication or separate-model retirement settles the retired spinner immediately; obsolete success, failure and finally cannot publish or clear a newer request's loading state. Codex catalog requests reuse a recent version lookup, including failures. Expired lookups retain the highest valid stable release seen. A replayable Codex catalog request retries one incomplete successful response. Send failures, intact HTTP errors and invalid JSON settle immediately.
discovery.assumptions: Upstream catalog contents and availability are inputs; finite two-request/context interleavings; HTTP schemas are checked by implementation tests. CatalogDiscoveryOwnership adds two roles, at most two issued requests per role and one selective invalidation per role, success/failure inputs and independent/shared modes. Shared mode projects polish publication/invalidation; independent assistant invalidation is checked in independent mode. Auth/context/unmount remain AsyncSettings obligations. TLC counterexample schedules replay actual hook APIs; this is bounded correspondence, not source refinement. Queued callback cancellation remains implementation-test coverage only; this companion has no scheduler/automatic-dispatch state and makes no queued-cancellation proof claim. ModelCatalogLoadingOwnership bounds two requests and one retirement by context, missing authentication or separate-mode closure, plus optional eligibility restoration. Request completion success/failure and order are environmental inputs. Hook and real picker regressions check credential deletion, OAuth sign-out, separate-mode closure/reopen and current completion. Debounce durations and UI rendering remain implementation-test obligations; this bounded model is not compiler refinement. CodexCatalogVersion models two readers sharing one process-local mutex, three ordered stable releases and a TTL of two ticks. Finish records a completed lookup. Transport, HTTP, schema and release-validation failures share one input. Rust tests check numeric parsing, the real cache owner and the exact TTL boundary. CatalogBodyRetry models one fetch call with seven possible read outcomes, a provider policy bit and request cloneability. Authentication recovery outside that call and response timing are outside its bounds.

oauth.obligation: Browser/device/refresh owners must remain current; logout and newer login reject old commits and stale fatal refresh.
oauth.assumptions: Identity-provider authentication and cryptography are trusted; generation counters must not wrap; storage durability is a separate obligation.

keys.obligation: Failed keyring write/delete is returned before publishing runtime caches; missing deletes are idempotent; saves, lazy loads and startup restore serialize storage and cache publication. Assistant delayed edits and retry retain captured provider; actual writes serialize; newest provider/read/edit ownership controls read publication. Polish credential reads never write storage; edits capture their provider and retain dirty drafts across switches and failed saves. Retired reads cannot publish. Vision credential provider switches preserve captured pending drafts, writes serialize, and read ownership includes provider, switch, edit version and the dirty-at-read snapshot.
keys.assumptions: Single keyring operations are atomic; physical OAuth multi-store commits are modeled separately. Getter failure is an unavailable credential, never proof of deletion. Companion model bounds two edits, two provider switches, two independent reads, success/failure and one retry per edit. UI/keyring promises and provider callbacks are checked with actual SettingsPage fixtures; native keyring internals are trusted. Read eligibility snapshots both the dirty draft and request/edit ownership: failed writes retain drafts; only matching successful writes clear them; a read started while dirty cannot become publishable after that clearing. Initial hydration is outside the companion; each provider switch captures a read before subsequent edits or matching save-clear transitions. The same abstract editor ownership machine applies independently to polish and assistant editors; cross-editor last-write ordering is supplied by keyring primitives. Initial profile hydration is tested in the implementation, not added to this companion model. VisionCredentialOwnership adds two edits, two reads, two provider switches and one retry per failed latest edit for Cerebras/OpenAI representatives. Switch flush queues the captured draft; one real write runs at a time. A read begun while dirty stays retired after save clears the draft. Keyring operations are trusted primitives; debounce timing and actual SettingsPage interaction are implementation tests, not a compiler refinement theorem.

profile-save.obligation: Each profile update queues its own current version under the same ordering lock; settled disk is latest.
profile-save.assumptions: Debounce timer and atomic filesystem replacement eventually succeed for settlement; Lean proves version ordering over arbitrary Nat updates. Failed writes and generation-owned status/retry are covered by isolated real-filesystem implementation tests; ProfilePersistence models successful writes only. The UI receives revisioned status snapshots after listener registration.

preferences.obligation: Settings controls require a successfully loaded profile; failures retain the blocked state and retry restores saved preferences. Normalize/validate before publication; optional clears are explicit; runtime-only flags do not overwrite other fields.
preferences.assumptions: The valid/invalid abstraction is instantiated by actual validators and unit partitions; it is not a proof of every Rust string/parser branch. The UI workload uses one representative History field, two profile reads, and success/failure inputs; other command workloads start ready and retain the full field partition.

providers.obligation: Custom provider fields validate before mutation; removed provider references resolve to safe existing roles; every LLM/catalog request freezes provider, endpoint and auth choice, and account credentials are resolved from one session.
providers.assumptions: URL parser and provider network behavior are trusted; built-in/custom represent equivalent reference classes, not all server features.

personalization.obligation: Blocked hotwords cannot be relearned automatically; concurrent user corrections survive automatic review; exported data excludes credentials.
personalization.assumptions: Canonical text normalization, JSON schema and learned suggestions are input partitions; explicit user imports/removals may replace user rules.

app-rules.obligation: First matching enabled rule wins; inheritance uses baseline; source window context stays captured.
app-rules.assumptions: Matching predicates are inputs; Lean proves first-match selection for arbitrary rule counts, TLC checks two rules and values.

routing.obligation: Off stays off; explicit actions execute; unknown Auto answers fail open; no-search and captured-window decisions are respected.
routing.assumptions: Classifier/model answers are Yes/No/Unknown inputs; linguistic quality is not proved. Screen and polish overrides are independent variables.

assistant.obligation: Current task owns cancellation; old completion cannot clear it; routed external search/screen preparation joins before dispatch; fresh screen payload uses the foreground snapshot sampled after preparation; only assistant workflow emits chat, validated sources can open. Initial-request retry success, failure and finally may change text, phase or busy state only while the captured session and generation still own the overlay; close retires ownership even within the same session.
assistant.assumptions: Network response content and browser opening are trusted external outcomes; request timeout/scheduler progress is required. Integrated search represents external third-party preparation; ModelNative tools run inside the LLM request. Joined preparation remains inside the cancellable assistant future. Foreground identity is sampled after preparation; OS changes after that read are not prevented. Integrated fresh screen preparation is modeled; reused pre-polish descriptions retain prior semantics and have Rust regression evidence. AssistantRetryOwnership bounds two retries, one retirement by a newer dictation or overlay close, and an optional same-session reopen. Streamed final publication and command settlement are independent inputs. Generation counters do not wrap; current completion remains permitted. This is bounded UI ownership correspondence, not compiler refinement.

selection.obligation: Replacement requires exact selection version, text and source window; cancellation owns latest task; raw selection is preserved. Disabling the listener retires pending capture epochs before cancellation/hide completes. The same publication lock covers eligibility, screenshot cache and the actual show_selection call; re-enabling never revives a retired worker.
selection.assumptions: OS selection and paste operations are external; two context versions represent arbitrary text, not recognition correctness. State changes use a window-targeted event after publication plus a post-subscription bootstrap snapshot; listener failure falls back to single-flight slow snapshots, checked by implementation tests. SelectionPublicationOwnership bounds two workers, finite epochs 0/1 and one disable/re-enable cycle, with optional screenshots and arbitrary capture completion order. Runtime epochs must not wrap. Retirement and the actual publication closure share one lock, including screenshot cache and native window publication. Native clipboard, screenshot and window primitives are trusted inputs; owner API tests plus source review establish correspondence, not compiler refinement or Windows runtime proof.

clipboard.obligation: Paste restores clipboard only when clipboard still contains the text owned by that paste; assistant output is never auto-pasted. A completed dictation remains a distinct session/text/original-target queue item while a second assistant occupies the recording slot; all eligible terminal paths schedule a drain; unknown/changed targets and paste failures expose original text for recovery.
clipboard.assumptions: OS clipboard reads/writes and key injection may fail; success means the API acknowledged the operation, not that a foreign application consumed it. Companion output model starts with A processing and independently records B starting/recording. It checks success/error/start-cancel/start-error exits and one focus change. Real queue/controller replay injects only the native paste primitive; source wiring tests establish terminal scheduling correspondence. OS focus remains sampled, and foreign-app consumption is not proved. One production finalizer owns each unique recording session. Tracked outputs deduplicate pending and in-flight IDs until their completion receipt settles; the legacy untracked push deduplicates pending IDs only and permits re-enqueue after a drain. There is no permanent global exactly-once ledger.

history.obligation: Persist only with consent; terminal output and paste authorization precede archive encoding and persistence; raw samples are snapshotted before ASR drains them, only with consent; history persistence and actual paste completion settle independently, and measured output timing updates only the inserted row ID; transactions are atomic; shared referenced/leased audio survives GC; reprocess retains captured source. After each SQL transaction, each audio lease count equals the number of independent holders; releasing the first of two shared holders must retain the second. History filter effects retire obsolete requests before debounce dispatch; pending or failed resets block old-offset pagination, current errors remain visible, and retry replaces from offset zero. Audio GC holds one SQLite write transaction across both ownership reads and filesystem unlink. Reprocess, successful delete and missing-row delete refresh the currently visible filter rather than the mutation-start callback.
history.assumptions: SQLite transactions and successful filesystem deletion are trusted primitives; detailed base bound of five rows, three audio classes and one reprocessor/count-one lease; DB errors retain audio conservatively. Terminal transcription/outcome publication and paste authorization precede archive work. Actual successful paste publishes an independent session-scoped timing event; persistence proceeds while a paste is queued, and later completion updates the inserted row ID without recreating deleted rows. Publication here means terminal transcription/subtitle results and paste authorization; assistant stream chunks and stream done arrive during LLM work and are excluded. Scheduling permits archive I/O and actual paste completion to settle independently after terminal publication; the model does not prove a wall-clock speedup. HistoryRecords retains its detailed five-row, three audio-class, single-reprocessor/count-one bound. HistoryLeaseInterleavings adds two independent tasks and two shared audio identities; release is DELETE count=1, UPDATE count>1, then commit. Equality is asserted outside the transaction; row deletion and GC interleave only at commit boundaries. Statistics reuse is checked by implementation tests: a retained read connection compares SQLite data_version, aggregate and latency queries share a read transaction, and concurrent changes invalidate cache publication. Database path remains fixed during the process; replacing the open database file is outside this contract. HistoryFilterOwnership adds seed row 1, optional old page row 2, one filter epoch, reset/retry replacement rows 3 and 4, and one normal pagination append row 5. Request identities are old=1/reset=2/retry=3/page=4; repeated retries fold to identity 3. Pagination availability directly follows hasMore, loading and error, independent of the specification pending-reset intent; normal pagination must use the current page epoch and offset two, while reset/retry use offset zero. Native success/failure are inputs. Effect retirement and debounce dispatch are distinct actions; actual replay checks 179/180 ms and public DOM/API behavior. Bounded correspondence only; no source refinement. HistoryAudioGcOwnership bounds one shared audio identity, two independent tasks and three GC attempts, including query/unlink failure. Initially saved paths are fresh and unique; existing-audio reprocessing uses leases. SQLite IMMEDIATE write exclusion, native filesystem operations and successful transaction commits are trusted primitives. The lock spans reference read, lease read and unlink; ownership query failures conservatively retain audio. HistoryMutationFilterOwnership bounds one mutation (polish, ASR, removed delete or missing delete), an A-to-B filter switch, a successful B load and success/failure of mutation and refresh. Bounded models and reviewed implementation tests are not compiler refinement.

windows.obligation: Only current show/hide generations publish; interactive state requires a window; exit signals capture and reaps child.
windows.assumptions: Tauri/Windows window placement and pixel geometry are native outcomes; selection drag/resize is reviewed native delegation, not a pixel-layout proof.

subtitles.obligation: Payloads belong to the current session; late interim cannot undo final; stable/tentative text and offsets must validate.
subtitles.assumptions: Text itself is abstract; driver/ASR model accuracy is external; rendering animations are covered by UI tests, not formal timing proofs.

hotkeys.obligation: Registration roles stay unique; backend follows classification; duplicate presses and stale stop owners cannot stop newer recording.
hotkeys.assumptions: OS key delivery/debounce clock are inputs; all three event kinds get separate configurations; bounded representative registration permutations are explicit.

transport.obligation: Request IDs are required; cancelled replies are ignored; streams validate identity, offsets, prefix, terminal output and sample bounds. One total command deadline covers stdin write, flush and reply read; timeout or cancellation invalidates the owned process and releases the command lock. OpenRouter maps unified reasoning before model heuristics; optional completion limits are omitted; native Anthropic retains its mandatory budget and bounded compatibility fallback. A single 120-second outer polish/edit operation budget covers preparation and all fallback attempts; explicit cancellation drops the active operation without treating sender cleanup as a user cancellation.
transport.assumptions: Current bundled servers echo request_id; older incompatible engines need updating. Clock/scheduler/network timeout fairness required; providers may fail. Write/flush/read phases use a three-tick total deadline; successful I/O progress never resets it. Real child-pipe replay checks blocked write, write progress before deadline and cancellation, then installs a fresh server. Scheduler/clock fairness and OS pipe semantics remain environmental assumptions. LlmRequestParameters abstracts validated provider/host classification and recognized parameter errors; live provider defaults/limits are external, with request-capture regressions establishing correspondence. The complete polish/edit deadline and dropped-future marker cleanup are established by paused-clock implementation tests, not a new source-level formal proof; synchronous OS calls remain environmental operations.

updater.obligation: Update versions compare by the actual numeric parser; release opening accepts HTTPS GitHub hosts only and reports errors.
updater.assumptions: GitHub release metadata and parsed version components are input partitions; numeric comparison is not a SemVer compliance claim.

ui-preferences.obligation: Theme follows system only in system mode; autostart reports success only after an authoritative confirmation. Mounted theme consumers agree; system changes preserve manual choices and delivered storage preferences synchronize windows.
ui-preferences.assumptions: localStorage/media query/Tauri autostart are platform primitives; visuals/accessibility need UI tests. Failed initial autostart read does not establish a known value. The optional tray startup preference is bound to the abstract preference/profile contracts; login-argument and legacy-default behavior have implementation tests, not a proof of native Windows startup. ThemeSynchronization bounds two windows with two mounted consumers, coalesces delivery to the latest stored preference and applies the DOM atomically. Animation, storage exceptions and unmount cleanup use real hook regressions; there is no delivery liveness or source refinement claim.

gpu-idle.obligation: Enabling at startup or runtime starts an idle window; no unload during commands or native streams; readiness survives suspension; successful next commands reload; stale initial settings reads cannot overwrite edits.
gpu-idle.assumptions: Monotonic time and weakly fair timer/command completion; finite clocks in TLC and unbounded Nat policy in Lean. Native load/free success is an input, not a driver proof. AppWorkflow GpuIdle represents Qwen 0.6B and R2T2 recording as an active stream. Input focus/click ordering is checked by real user-event regression tests; linguistic accuracy is outside proof.

cuda-architecture-selection.obligation: Default CUDA builds preserve the upstream architecture sequence and append generic 80-real/90-real only when that exact virtual target lacks bare/native coverage. Changed plans require a second configure whose parsed report exactly matches the plan before compile/package; manifest records the actual report. Explicit overrides and CPU builds retain their established behavior.
cuda-architecture-selection.assumptions: Finite configure/verify/build/package protocol, with eleven representative generic, suffixed and future tokens and upstream sequences of length one to three, preserving duplicates and order. CPU uses an empty architecture sequence. Final configure results are environmental inputs: matching, stale, changed or invalid. Three fault controls omit native additions, drop upstream PTX or accept a stale final report. Offline regressions replay the real Python main entry with synthetic CMake reports, actual runtime copying and manifest creation; configure failure/error-log parsing are implementation-test obligations. This is bounded protocol and implementation correspondence, not Python source refinement, CMake/compiler/driver correctness, binary cubin inspection, universal toolkit/GPU compatibility or performance proof.

exact-head-selection.obligation: A marked four-column F16/F32 head uses one immutable per-context K/vocabulary decision. Grouped requires complete initial parity and finite positive event samples with at least 5% improvement; capture misses, ineligible requests and different keys use scalar execution without tuning. Calibration always ends by executing the selected output; fresh contexts may calibrate again; CUDA API errors remain terminal.
exact-head-selection.assumptions: Two contexts and two abstract K/vocabulary keys; four-column requests only, two calls per context for policy and three across at most two lifetimes for restart. One eligible application head per backend context; serialized synchronous application commands and idle-lock exclusion. Actual stock-kernel/device/layout guards narrow eligibility. Other column counts retain their actual scalar shape outside this model. Calibration effects/ticks are conservative abstract observations; native parity rejection skips timing. First-input parity is not all-input arithmetic proof. No compiler/driver refinement, unrestricted concurrent C ABI calls, universal GPU validation or performance proof.

saved-engine-invalidation.obligation: Successful native engine setters emit saved-configuration invalidation after the backend transition. Initial authoritative reads follow listener acquisition, with visible failure fallback. Delivered events retire earlier settings reads and GUI continuations; only current saved-state reads may publish, retain loading ownership or refresh model status. Unknown identity blocks credential edits, current failures remain visible, user drafts survive old key reads, and retired listeners release their subscription.
saved-engine-invalidation.assumptions: AsrAgentSettings bounds two external events/reads, one GUI engine-or-region mutation, two effect owners and nonwrapping epochs; local reads, GUI promises and listener registration eventually settle under weak fairness. It begins with delivered invalidations; native emission ordering and delivery remain source/native correspondence obligations, not an event-bus proof. AsrSubscriptionBootstrap separates native installation, JS acknowledgment, writes, emissions, snapshots and completions for one engine field. Three positive workloads contain exactly zero, one or two sequential writes and one, two or three reads respectively. Their union covers stopping after each write count; weak fairness completes only each profile's scheduled work. The single mount may dispose; failed registration reports a diagnostic and hydrates once. Multi-field transactions, overlapping writers and engine/model correctness are outside this bootstrap model. The coupled transition, invalidation and effect-replay combination is not formally qualified. Hook tests mock Tauri and local storage; native host tests are a separate surface. These path-qualified models are checked by the separate required CLI contracts job, not the application runner runs/actions matrix or its check_model_bindings loop. Registry anchor validation alone does not establish property activation, reachability, completed model matrices or final source/model correspondence.

agent-cli.obligation: Target/configuration precedence and local-engine validation precede acquisition. Desktop sessions reuse one owned broker, correlate replies, retain explicit backend failures, stop without queued reads or retry after fatal transport failure, and reap only their owned child. Frozen/bootstrap resources, native thread options and doctor diagnostics retain their declared boundaries. Preserve decoded admitted JSON string contents across the Python client/backend byte protocol, including escaped unpaired surrogates; unsupported backend values may be rejected without silent client-side replacement. Desktop-bound invalid scalar strings and exact physical serialized records over 65536 bytes fail before broker acquisition/write; session input errors retain caller IDs, the live owner and continuation.
agent-cli.assumptions: Each companion retains its own finite input partitions, acquisition/response/cleanup steps and local-step fairness; command sessions contain at most two records. Python children in unit tests are synthetic JSONL fixtures. Model inference, live desktop behavior, unrestricted concurrent callers and native dependency correctness need separate evidence. These path-qualified models are checked by the separate required CLI contracts job, not the application runner runs/actions matrix or its check_model_bindings loop. Registry anchor validation alone does not establish property activation, reachability, completed model matrices or final source/model correspondence. UnicodeSerialization bounds five representative strings at key/value positions and abstracts JSON syntax/recursive containers. No native serde/ASR acceptance, arbitrary Unicode sequence, size or progress proof; response fields and signed external identity are executable controls. DesktopAdmission is an additional generic application runs/actions matrix entry: one-shot or two session records, optional prior live owner at internal sequence 8/9, physical LF/CRLF widths and scalar/escaped-size partitions. Its Guard maps to validate_desktop_request in reviewed CLI SHA256 d1a9f86c0bcc3419ad7f1b1872a24a7e44d11bb552bb0860eda34f67884ac09b; main and run_session validate app payloads before acquisition/send, while engine, doctor and local exit bypass it. Existing companions retain their own narrower contracts: admitted app dispatch assumes this separate scalar/size guard, Session invalid input refines its recoverable bad_fields branch, and UnicodeSerialization still covers unchanged direct-client/engine serialization. See formal/cli/README.md for each model correspondence. This source review is not a current TLC receipt or a native decoder proof.

agent-transport.obligation: A private endpoint is published under one stable host lease. Authenticated bounded frames preserve server identity and request correlation, validate before dispatch, and retain absolute ingress/client/egress deadlines. Worker slots remain owned through actual dispatch and egress; shutdown drains admitted work, removes only its endpoint and releases the lease after cleanup. The stdin broker flushes readiness and replies, keeps exit local, and stops before another read after terminal failure.
agent-transport.assumptions: The models abstract Windows ACL/filesystem primitives, HMAC authenticity and nonce freshness, finite workers/frames and eventually returning local dispatch/I/O/cleanup. Concrete authenticated native packets, ACLs, byte limits and controlled native socket-write schedules require the source-importing Rust harnesses. No cryptographic proof, arbitrary dispatch timeout or kernel-backpressure guarantee is implied. These path-qualified models are checked by the separate required CLI contracts job, not the application runner runs/actions matrix or its check_model_bindings loop. Registry anchor validation alone does not establish property activation, reachability, completed model matrices or final source/model correspondence.

agent-host.obligation: The headless desktop host and GUI register the same managed controller boundary. Recording, Processing, native ownership and invalid input exclude incompatible effects; admitted operations retain their lease until settlement. Observed runtime identity/stats come from native replies, explicit empty transcripts remain valid silence, and missing transcripts/backend errors remain visible. Client exit leaves the host running; owner shutdown retires starts, cancels/reaps owned work and cleans owned audio before releasing resources.
agent-host.assumptions: AppQuery bounds two callers and one native owner; AgentHost bounds two clients, two operations and two start/restart attempts with two engine identities. Native replies and local process reap are environmental inputs under declared fairness. Managed-state tests use MockRuntime and synthetic native children; the headless host recipe separately drives an explicitly supplied own-build executable. Neither establishes live GUI event delivery, microphones, models or provider behavior. These path-qualified models are checked by the separate required CLI contracts job, not the application runner runs/actions matrix or its check_model_bindings loop. Registry anchor validation alone does not establish property activation, reachability, completed model matrices or final source/model correspondence. RuntimeConfiguration is an additional exception executed by the generic application runs/actions matrix: two runtime actions, two local identities plus cloud/raw-unknown classes, and one optional configuration writer while dispatch waits on lifecycle. Raw unknown values normalize to the default local engine. This is the validated Stage A lifecycle-before-ASR checkpoint, where a pending CLI request owns no ASR lease; no third ASR owner is present. The actor acquires ASR before an allowlisted write, settles its owned stop/reap with false readiness, releases ASR, then releases lifecycle. Starting the actor is optional; once started, successful actor stop/reap and internal settlement are assumed fair. CLI restart invocation, pending stop with lifecycle held and no reply, successful stop settlement, and explicit lifecycle release are separate actions. Actor and CLI stop settlement have independent typed temporal sensitivity controls. Prefix completion ends at rejection or transfer to common startup, with no accepted response projected at transfer; common service completion, final reply, provider behavior, post-transfer configuration changes and wall-clock bounds remain outside scope.

cli-delivery.obligation: Only a verified CLI artifact matching original source/package inputs may replace the previous executable; failed builds preserve unrelated files and release owned staging. Release selection requires a nonempty artifact. Publication requires local checks plus all six named CI jobs on the frozen SHA, post-fetch HEAD/remote/clean observations, and an explicit candidate tag before release creation.
cli-delivery.assumptions: One artifact builder, two input revisions, atomic filesystem replacement and eventual local cleanup. ReleaseGate models one candidate and assumes an exclusive publisher with no external writes after the final observations through tagging; it does not make those observations atomic across Git/GitHub. Tests execute controlled local boundaries, not remote publication or NSIS installation. These path-qualified models are checked by the separate required CLI contracts job, not the application runner runs/actions matrix or its check_model_bindings loop. Registry anchor validation alone does not establish property activation, reachability, completed model matrices or final source/model correspondence.

entrypoint-routing-observation.obligation: Verification support: admit only the reviewed source identity, observe explicit-empty client routing and the original/minimized desktop boundary before GUI construction, and remove the test-only overlay on valid restoration. Exact predicate inversions must violate their expected observation.
entrypoint-routing-observation.assumptions: Test-only observation, not a live GUI claim. Three input partitions are explicit-empty client, normal desktop and minimized desktop; absent data is excluded. Identity is the complete existing 21-pin/variant/path conjunction. No scheduler, provider, native process or arbitrary argv proof is claimed. The generic application formal matrix executes the original routing positive and two predicate-inversion cases; registry anchors alone do not establish actual TLC completion.

entrypoint-prepared-provenance.obligation: Verification support: matching reviewed content admits any well-formed prepared owner HEAD, records that actual HEAD in the overlay receipt, and requires current owner/receipt equality plus all identity gates before launch admission or restore. Rejected helper calls perform no writes or launch admission.
entrypoint-prepared-provenance.assumptions: Two valid HEAD partitions and one invalid partition; one apply, at most one owner edit, one receipt edit and one identity loss between invocations, then one verify or restore. Each helper call is exclusive and synchronous with successful filesystem operations. Complete stage-specific identity and app/fixture checks are Boolean conjunctions, not removed concrete gates. verify_launch returns read-only admission metadata and does not launch a process. No intra-call TOCTOU, partial-I/O/crash durability, cryptographic metadata authentication, live Git validation, repeated calls or native application execution is proved. The generic application formal matrix checks the positive configuration, four semantic controls and six reachability witnesses; witnesses are not safety-mutant kills.

cli-command-entry.obligation: The installed Windows console entry discovers the neighboring or parent desktop executable without selecting itself. Installer command publication copies the console CLI before adding one own user-PATH entry, preserves raw unrelated PATH tokens, rejects preexisting reparse points and removes only its own command entry and alias during uninstall. The caller decides process-close cancellation or failure before command cleanup; denial preserves the existing alias and own PATH entry. Each serialized operation settles under returning OS calls.
cli-command-entry.assumptions: Two serialized install/uninstall calls, initially empty command ownership, representative ordered foreign tokens including empty and expandable entries, and a fixed preexisting reparse-point choice. Normal, missing-source, copy-error and registry-write-error outcomes and caller process-close admission/denial are bounded inputs. Admission remains valid until cleanup; an external desktop restart between the hook and template's repeated guard is excluded. Weak fairness assumes synchronous OS calls return. Uncooperative external concurrent PATH/filesystem writers, process crashes, permanently blocked OS calls, native PE/argument/stdio behavior, remaining NSIS wiring and environment broadcast are outside this finite model. Real PowerShell tests exercise owned temporary registry keys/files, not the real HKCU Environment entrypoint; Python discovery tests use a synthetic broker. The fresh-VM native installer smoke and hook source-order regression are distinct evidence and do not execute the interactive cancellation prompt. PowerShell/NSIS/native branch coverage and source mutation remain unmeasured. This is reviewed source/model correspondence, not compiler refinement or a whole-installer proof.

r2t2-chunk-cadence.obligation: CPU uses fixed 320 ms, CUDA uses a fixed 160 ms Python input grain. ABI 0.6+ opted-in rolling CUDA doubles the native decode grain only after the first visible preview and keeps it until the segment ends. Reset or a new segment starts at 160 ms. Finish drains both Python and native real-audio remainders once. Rolling coalesced finish pads the frontend's private input to the smallest complete configured block after trimming, capping the block at 320 ms. Public and logical sample counts exclude this model-only padding.
r2t2-chunk-cadence.assumptions: One model unit is 80 ms. Up to ten units arrive, one Python input grain or less per Feed, for already admitted speech. The decoder may publish or retract speculative text. Reset represents cancellation followed by a new start. The live and file server paths disable the maximum segment limit. Pause abstracts a silence-triggered segment finish followed by the next admitted segment; final synthetic context is excluded from real-sample accounting. The opt-in CUDA test observes actual native partial-result availability at each 160 ms push. Oversized VAD pre-roll, acoustic content, decoder quality, device timing and failing DLL calls are outside the bounded model. The final-window model separately covers empty and small inputs and both sides of the 16 s rolling-window limit. It assumes a synchronous successful decode with a retained commit boundary at or before the 8 s trim target. Base grains span 80, 160, 240, 320 and 640 ms. The model checks frame accounting. The native source fixture checks interleaved PCM values, configured durations and nearest-frame rounding.

qwen-preview-cadence.obligation: The Qwen3-ASR preview cadence adapts to the capture length: 1920 samples for the first preview, 3200 below 64000 samples (4 s) and 5120 from 64000 samples on, decided at the end of every _accept_pcm from the sample count that accept produced - never from the previous block's count. A replaced or cancelled preview job never publishes, finish() reuses the published text only when it covers the whole capture and the capture fits window_samples, otherwise the full capture is decoded, and reset() returns the startup state.
qwen-preview-cadence.assumptions: Thresholds 1/2/3 and cutoff 4 preserve production ordering without a fixed samples-per-unit ratio. Each capture step adds one or two units, up to ten, with an eight-unit window. One live job and nonempty publications are modelled. Launch abstracts replacement of a queued snapshot in _submit or a prepared snapshot when the next preparation completes. The model omits overlapping jobs, suppression and thread scheduling. The base-class finish rule reuses published text covering the capture inside the window. The pipeline can also reuse an exact in-flight job, exercised by test_qwen_pipeline.py#test_feed_acknowledges_during_native_and_only_latest_pending_runs. Five safety controls cover stale publication, incomplete or out-of-window finish reuse, frozen thresholds and lagged threshold decisions. The separate witness requires a new queued job to identify the earlier job it replaced. These finite checks do not establish runtime latency.
